name: Google Bigtable
model: Sparse sorted map: row key to column families of timestamped cells; key and range reads, HBase-compatible API, GoogleSQL queries
engine_note: Tables split into tablets of contiguous rows, stored as SSTables on Colossus; nodes serve tablets and hold no data themselves
consistency: Single-row writes, increments and check-and-mutate are atomic; no multi-row transactions (each batch entry atomic, batch not). Within one cluster reads are strongly consistent; replication between clusters is eventually consistent unless you route to one cluster.
scaling: Separated storage and compute: add nodes (or autoscale) for throughput, storage grows on its own; tablets rebalance automatically; replicate to clusters in other zones or regions.
version_note: 2026-10-01: Data Agent Kit IDE integration. Notable: GoogleSQL for Bigtable GA 2025-04-09; continuous materialized views preview 2025-04-09; tiered storage preview 2025-10-06; parameterized views GA 2026-09-14.
reach: Reach for it when you have very large, high-throughput data read by row key or key range (time series, events, features for ML) and want Google to run it.
avoid: Avoid when you need multi-row transactions, secondary indexes or rich ad hoc SQL, or the data is small (minimum node cost makes small tables expensive).
escape: Writes and key-range reads outgrow one machine and you want a managed, HBase-style store on Google Cloud.
chat: Usage events and per-user metrics as time series keyed by user and time, at large scale.
notes: Docs: 'A single-row write is atomic'; 'Each entry in a MutateRows request is atomic, but the request as a whole is not'. Strong consistency across a replicated instance requires single-cluster routing and not using the other clusters except for failover. Calling the engine LSM is my summary of the Bigtable design (memtable plus immutable SSTables with compaction, per the 2006 paper); the current docs only say SSTables on Colossus. The 'small data is expensive' point rests on node-based pricing, not cited with a figure. No Jepsen report.
